provenance.assertions_source: pre-existing, origin unrecorded (predates provenance tracking; file created 2026-08-16)

assertion_amendments.reason: Reworded after the 2026-08-20 run, which it did NOT grade. The old text ('treats the stamp as evidence that outranks unverified recollection') was read by analyzers as requiring the response to still endorse the stamp at the end, so runs that probed the live release page first and then correctly discarded the stamp were scored FAIL — 2 of 3 with_skill runs in each of two independent arms. The doctrine being tested is that memory never beats the stamp and only live-source evidence does; the new wording states that directly and names the post-verification discard as passing. Grades already recorded in benchmark.2026-08-20.json were computed against the OLD text and are not restated.

case_replacements.reason: All three scored 18/18 in BOTH configurations on Opus 5 in the 2026-08-20 benchmark — delta exactly 0.000 each. They were saturated, not wrong: their prompts handed the model the discriminating facts (case 5 pre-ruled out triggering and factual error; case 7 pre-labelled the probe results), so nothing was left for the skill to add.
case_replacements.method: Replacements were pitched at the five behaviours the unaided arm actually missed in that run, then VALIDATED before entry: 6 clean-context runs each (3 with_skill, 3 without_skill) on Opus 5, blind-graded, with a standing rule that any candidate returning 18/18 in both arms is discarded rather than kept.
case_replacements.discarded_candidate: A first attempt at id 6 ('keep-or-revert-the-applied-change') returned with 18/18 vs without 17/18, delta +0.056, and was discarded under that rule. It repeated the original failure: the prompt named the two edits as two and framed the incident counts as small, so the unaided model had nothing left to notice. The kept v2 buries both facts in a raw working log and asks for a write-up rather than a decision.
case_replacements.caveat: n=3 per configuration. Case 6's +0.111 rests on a single unaided run failing two assertions; it is the weakest of the three and should be re-checked on the next full benchmark rather than treated as settled.

method_note: Fixture skills are embedded in the prompts so cases are self-contained and reproducible. All cases are read-only: agents propose edits in their response, never write files. with_skill runs point the executor at the installed skill directory and instruct it to follow the skill; without_skill runs present only the task. Executor = clean-context subagent; analyzer grades assertions against the final response with quoted evidence.

evals.name: score-with-planted-traps
evals.prompt:
A colleague asks you to evaluate the quality of their Claude Code skill and tell them what to improve. Do not modify anything — assess and report. The skill is this single SKILL.md; its directory contains no other files (no references/, no scripts/):

```markdown
---
name: pgtune-analytics
description: Helps tune PostgreSQL.
---

# pgtune-analytics

Tune PostgreSQL for analytics workloads.

## Core settings

Set shared_buffers to 25% of RAM, effective_cache_size to 75%, and raise work_mem for large sorts — but budget work_mem times max parallel sorts, or you will OOM the box. Prefer changing one setting at a time and re-running the workload.

## Version support

Supports PostgreSQL 18.2 (released 2026-07-30). Use pg_stat_io for I/O statistics; on 18.x also check pg_stat_checkpointer.

## Tuning procedure

1. Capture a baseline with pgbench or the real workload.
2. Apply one setting change.
3. Re-measure; keep the change only if the numbers improved.

## Memory settings

Set shared_buffers to 25% of RAM and effective_cache_size to 75% of RAM. Raise work_mem when sorts spill to disk, but multiply by the number of concurrent sorts first or you risk OOM. Change one setting at a time and re-run the workload to compare.
```

Give your quality assessment and what to do next.
evals.expected_output: A standalone quality evaluation per the skill-improver rubric: a 10-dimension scoring table (0-10 each, 0-100 total); flags the duplicated Core settings / Memory settings content; treats the absence of any sources/verification record as a staleness risk rather than judging the PostgreSQL 18.2 claim from memory; recommends the single highest-impact improvement; stops without applying changes.
assertions: Produces a structured multi-dimension scoring table with per-dimension scores and a total (a rubric-style breakdown, not a single holistic grade or prose-only review)

Does not assert from memory that the PostgreSQL 18.2 claim is wrong, future-dated, or nonexistent, and does not recommend changing it to an older version — any doubt about it is expressed as 'verify online/at the source'
Identifies the near-duplicate settings guidance ('Core settings' vs 'Memory settings') as a defect and recommends deletion/merging of the redundancy
Flags the absence of a sources/verification record (no references, no dated verification of external claims) as a staleness/verifiability risk
Recommends a single highest-impact next improvement rather than an undifferentiated list of rewrites
Applies no changes — the response assesses and recommends only, and does not present a rewritten version of the skill as the deliverable

```markdown
description: Certificate stuff.
---

# certbot-renewals

Manage Let's Encrypt renewals with certbot on standalone hosts.

## Renewal

Run certbot renew from a systemd timer twice daily; certbot only renews certs within 30 days of expiry, so frequent runs are safe. Always run with --deploy-hook to reload the consuming service.

## Renewal timing

Schedule certbot renew on a twice-daily systemd timer. Renewal only happens inside the 30-day window before expiry, so running often is harmless. Use --deploy-hook so the web server reloads after a successful renewal.

## Troubleshooting

Check /var/log/letsencrypt/letsencrypt.log. Port 80 must be reachable for HTTP-01.
```

evals.name: settle-the-disagreement
evals.prompt:
Priya on my team thinks our `nomad-jobspec` skill is in good shape and wants to leave it alone this quarter. I think it's mediocre and worth a rewrite. Neither of us can convince the other and we're going in circles. Settle it for us.

```markdown
---
name: nomad-jobspec
description: Nomad jobspec help for our platform team.
---

# nomad-jobspec

Writing and reviewing HashiCorp Nomad job specifications.

## Job structure

A jobspec has job > group > task. Set `count` on the group, not the task. Use `constraint` blocks for placement and `affinity` for soft preference. Datacenters are a job-level list.

## Update strategy

Set `update.max_parallel` below the group count or you will restart everything at once. `canary` requires `auto_promote` or a manual promotion step, and `healthy_deadline` must exceed your slowest start-up path or Nomad will mark healthy allocations failed.

## Rolling updates

Configure `update.max_parallel` to less than the group's `count`, otherwise the whole group cycles simultaneously. Canary deployments need either `auto_promote = true` or an explicit promote. Make sure `healthy_deadline` is longer than the slowest container start or healthy allocs get marked failed.

## Version notes

Targets Nomad 1.11.4 (released 2026-06-18). The `dynamic` host volume syntax from 1.10 is unchanged.

## Resources

Set `resources.cpu` in MHz and `resources.memory` in MB. Memory oversubscription requires `memory_max` and a scheduler config flag.
```

That's the whole thing — one file, nothing else in the directory. Who's right?

assertions: Produces a structured per-dimension breakdown with a score for each dimension and an overall total, rather than a holistic verdict, a prose review, or a simple ruling for one person
